domain_description: How students feel, what motivates them, and whether they experience themselves as agents in their own learning — belonging, autonomy, emotional literacy, self-efficacy, restorative practice, trauma-informed teaching. All interventions cross-referenced to peer-reviewed meta-analyses where one exists. We have curated the Manning catalogue here for relevance and evidence quality, leaving out skills where the research base was too thin to grade fairly.

skills.description: Design classroom culture so every student — including the ones who feel most on the edge — has reliable signals that they belong here, are seen as capable, and will be supported when things get hard. Relational routines, repair after conflict, identity-safe materials, and explicit anti-marginalisation moves rather than 'be kind' posters.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Social and emotional learning strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: No materials cost. The lift is sustained PD in relational practice (greeting, check-ins, repair after conflict, identity-safe framing), consistent classroom routines, and ideally whole-school alignment. Davies et al. found multi-tier programs (g=0.78) outperform single-classroom interventions — meaning the most effective version is a leadership decision, not just a teacher one.

skills.description: Diagnose which of the three Self-Determination Theory needs — autonomy, competence, relatedness — is undermet for a student or a class, then redesign the task to address it: meaningful choices, calibrated challenge, explicit rationale, and connection to peers' work instead of vague 'engagement' tweaks.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Teachers need working knowledge of the three SDT needs, diagnostic skill to spot which one is undermet, and the will to actually rework assignments — adding meaningful choices, calibrating challenge, articulating rationale. No materials cost; the lift is conceptual and habitual. Diagnostic step matters because generic 'autonomy' fixes (free choice) can backfire when competence is the real bottleneck.

skills.description: Run the RULER sequence — Recognise, Understand, Label, Express, Regulate — using the mood meter and classroom charter so students build emotional vocabulary and self-regulation strategies they can actually use, instead of generic 'feelings posters' that never get referenced again.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Social and emotional learning strand
skills.effect_d_source: Cipriano, Strambler, Naples, Ha, Kirk, Wood et al.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Full RULER fidelity includes Yale Center training and coaching (real PD cost) but lighter adoption — RULER acronym, mood meter, classroom charter — can be run by trained teachers without certification. Either way, emotional literacy needs sustained practice across the year, not a single 'feelings unit'. Cipriano et al. found SAFE programs (Sequenced, Active, Focused, Explicit) outperform less structured rollouts.
